To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrospun NiCr nanoparticles (NPs)–decorated carbon nanobundles (CNFs) have a high catalytic activity for the hydrolysis of ammonia borane.
NiCr alloy nanoparticles-decorated carbon nanofiber catalysts have been synthesized by a simple one-step thermal treatment.
NiCr alloy nanoparticles@carbon nanofibers have been synthesized by the electrospinning technique and used as a catalyst for the hydrogen release from the chemical hydrogen source ammonia borane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and utilization of the NiCr alloy nanoparticles-decorated carbon nanofiber as efficient and competent catalysts for the dehydrogenation reaction of ammonia borane.
a new approach for the fabrication of Ni1−xCrxCNFs with different compositions.
the fabrication and utilization as a catalyst of NiCr alloy NPs-decorated carbon nanofiber (CNF).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introduced catalyst is a promising candidate for the efficient hydrolytic deamination of ammonia borane at room temperature.

the introduction of the Ni1−xCr0.15 alloy nanoparticles into the electrospun CNFs has a positive effect on the catalytic performance, which is due to the presence of the NiCr alloy nanoparticles and the high specific surface area of the CNFs.

the introduction of Cr into Ni–CNFs is beneficial for the catalytic performance, which is attributed to the formation of Cr2Ni3, as well as the presence of the NiCr nanoparticles in the CNFs matrix, as confirmed by XRD, XPS, and SEM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrospun NiCr alloy nanoparticles@carbon nanofibers can be considered a competent non-precatalyst for the hydrolysis of ammonia borane.
this work is the first to report on the synthesis of NiCr alloy/CNFs as an efficient and competent nonprecious catalyst for the hydrolysis of ammonia borane at room temperature.
the introduction of Cr into the Ni–CNFs catalyst has a positive impact, which enhances the catalytic activity of Ni–CNFs for the hydrolysis of AB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NiCr alloy nanoparticles@carbon nanofibers can be a potential candidate for hydrogen generation applications from ammonia borane.
the introduction of Cr into Ni–CNFs can enhance the catalytic activity of AB dehydrogenations.

the Ni1−xCr0.15/CNFs can be used as an effective catalyst for the dehydrogenation reaction of AB, and this catalyst can be recycled for at least six cycles without significant loss of catalytic activity.
